newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ausmelt, Thyssen talk steel waste deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ausmelt, Thyssen talk steel waste deal.

text.p: Australia's Meekatharra Minerals Ltd and its strategic partner Ausmelt Ltd were negotiating with German steel group Thyssen AG for the supply of steel industry iron-bearing waste, Meekatharra's general manager Neill Arthur said on Thursday.
Arthur was commenting on statements made at an industry conference here by Ausmelt's deputy chairman John Floyd.
The two companies are in a strategic alliance which involves Meekatharra supplying low ash content steaming coal to future licensees of Ausmelt low-cost smelting technology.
Thyssen wanted to process about 200,000 tonnes of steel industry iron-bearing waste a year, Arthur said.
"It's not a contract yet but something we're working on, whether it's going to come off or not we don't know," Arthur told Reuters.
Meekatharra coal would be used in the project, he said.
Ausmelt technology so far has been used by Peruvian tin producer Minsur SA and Japan's Mitsui Mining and Smelting Co.
Meekatharra and Ausmelt each have a 40 percent stake in the proposed US$500 million pig iron project, under investigation for establishment in South Australia.
The steelmaking plant is proposed to be based on iron and coal resources in the north of the state, about 100 km south of Coober Pedy.
The pig iron project was definitely going ahead, Arthur said. Cost structures continued to demonstrate the project as among the cheapest in the world, he said.
Construction is to start soon on a demonstration plant soon while full commercial production is scheduled by year 2000.
